headline: An NHS doctor says an AI tool helped him spot that a vitamin B6 shortage may have caused his mother's life-threatening seizures, which stopped after a B6 dose.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 3: the case was first reported by the BBC on 1 Oct 2026 (the events date from May), the Times piece could not be read for new facts, and it is a single case.
importance_line: Parkinson's patients and their doctors may pay closer attention to vitamin B6 levels, but this is one case, the neurologist says only 14 similar cases have been reported, and trials are needed before practice changes.
summary: The BBC reported on 1 Oct 2026 that Ed Patrick, an NHS anaesthetist, used Google's Gemini AI tool to summarise recent medical research when his mother Ann, who has Parkinson's disease, was dying of continuous seizures in May, and told her neurologist that a vitamin B6 deficiency, possibly linked to her Parkinson's drug carbidopa-levodopa, may be the cause; an intravenous B6 dose then appeared to stop the seizures. Doctors quoted say clinical trials are needed and patients should not change their own medication, and The Times carried its own account of the case on 10 Oct 2026.
